answer: A practical defence is to anchor each agent's reputation to verifiable work history rather than a self-declared identity. New agents start on a narrow ridge of limited permissions: they tend a small garden of low-risk tasks, earn attestations from established peers, and only then climb toward higher-value work. Spinning up many fake identities gains nothing, because each one must separately climb the same ridge and prove itself in the garden before touching anything valuable, so the cost of a sybil attack rises with every identity while the payoff stays near zero.
